goty.label: Game of the Year
goty.description: The industry's biggest night. Every Game of the Year winner since the ceremony began.

winners.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
winners.description: A debut turn-based RPG that swept nine awards, the most in the show's history, with a painterly Belle Époque world and a soundtrack that became a phenomenon.

winners.title: Astro Bot
winners.description: A joyful 3D platformer and love letter to PlayStation history that proved pure play could still win the biggest prize.

winners.title: Baldur's Gate 3
winners.description: The Dungeons & Dragons RPG that redefined choice and consequence with an almost impossible amount of reactivity.

winners.title: Elden Ring
winners.description: Hidetaka Miyazaki and George R. R. Martin's open-world Souls epic: brutal, beautiful and endlessly discoverable.

winners.title: It Takes Two
winners.description: A co-op only adventure about a couple on the verge of divorce, packed with a new mechanic every ten minutes.

winners.title: The Last of Us Part II
winners.description: A divisive, devastating revenge story that pushed performance capture and narrative ambition to a new level.

winners.title: Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice
winners.description: A shinobi action game built around posture, parries and the most satisfying deflect in gaming.

winners.title: God of War
winners.description: Kratos reborn as a father in the Norse realms. One unbroken camera shot from start to finish.

winners.title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
winners.description: The open-air reinvention of Zelda that changed how a generation of open-world games think about freedom.

winners.title: Overwatch
winners.description: The hero shooter that turned a cast of colourful characters into a global esport and cosplay culture.

winners.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
winners.description: Geralt's final hunt. Still the benchmark for side quests that feel like main quests.

winners.title: Dragon Age: Inquisition
winners.description: The very first Game Awards winner: a sprawling fantasy RPG about holding a fractured world together.

anime.label: Anime of the Year
anime.description: The fan-voted Anime of the Year, plus the series that defined each season's conversation.

winners.title: My Hero Academia: Final Season
winners.description: The finale of Deku's journey took the top prize after a record 73 million global votes.

winners.title: Solo Leveling
winners.description: Sung Jinwoo's rise from the weakest hunter to the shadow monarch became a worldwide event.

winners.title: Jujutsu Kaisen Season 2
winners.description: The Shibuya Incident arc. The same year Frieren: Beyond Journey's End topped MyAnimeList's all-time ranking.

winners.title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners
winners.description: A neon tragedy set in Night City that reignited an entire video game's fanbase.

winners.title: Attack on Titan: Final Season
winners.description: Eren's rumbling begins. The series that turned a decade of mystery into a global finale.

winners.title: Jujutsu Kaisen
winners.description: Cursed energy, Gojo Satoru and a new shonen king. Vinland Saga won Best Drama the year before.

winners.title: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba
winners.description: Tanjiro's water breathing and ufotable's animation set a new visual bar for TV anime.

winners.title: Devilman Crybaby
winners.description: Masaaki Yuasa's fearless, heartbreaking reimagining of Go Nagai's classic.

winners.title: Made in Abyss
winners.description: A deceptively cute descent into one of anime's most beautiful and cruel worlds.

winners.title: Yuri!!! on Ice
winners.description: The very first Anime of the Year: figure skating, romance and MAPPA's arrival on the world stage.

tv.label: TV Show of the Year
tv.description: Television's highest honour for drama, year by year.

winners.title: The Pitt
winners.description: One fifteen-hour shift in a Pittsburgh emergency room, told in real time.

winners.title: Shōgun
winners.description: A feudal Japan epic that broke the record for most Emmy wins by a single season.

winners.title: Succession
winners.description: The Roy family's final, brutal season and a third Drama Series win.

winners.title: Succession
winners.description: Season three: boardroom warfare as Shakespearean tragedy.

winners.title: The Crown
winners.description: Netflix's first Drama Series win, for the Diana and Thatcher years.

winners.title: Succession
winners.description: The first of three wins for Jesse Armstrong's media-dynasty drama.

winners.title: Game of Thrones
winners.description: The controversial final season still took the top prize, a fourth Drama Series win.

winners.title: Game of Thrones
winners.description: Season seven: the dragons reach Westeros and the wall comes down.

winners.title: The Handmaid's Tale
winners.description: The first streaming series ever to win Outstanding Drama Series.

winners.title: Game of Thrones
winners.description: Battle of the Bastards, Hold the Door, and a record-setting Emmy haul.

winners.title: Game of Thrones
winners.description: The first fantasy series ever to win television's top drama award.

winners.title: Breaking Bad
winners.description: Walter White's final season: arguably the most acclaimed ending in television history.

movies.label: Movie of the Year
movies.description: Best Picture winners, listed by the year the film was released.

winners.title: One Battle After Another
winners.description: Paul Thomas Anderson's action-comedy odyssey took the top honour at the 2026 ceremony.

winners.title: Anora
winners.description: Sean Baker's screwball tragedy about a Brooklyn dancer and a Russian oligarch's son.

winners.title: Oppenheimer
winners.description: Nolan's three-hour biopic of the father of the atomic bomb became a billion-dollar event film.

winners.title: Everything Everywhere All at Once
winners.description: A multiverse family drama with hot-dog fingers that swept seven Oscars.

winners.title: CODA
winners.description: The first film from a streaming service to win Best Picture.

winners.title: Nomadland
winners.description: Frances McDormand on the road across the American West in a quiet, humane masterpiece.

winners.title: Parasite
winners.description: The first non-English-language film ever to win Best Picture.

winners.title: Green Book
winners.description: A road trip through the 1960s Deep South with Viggo Mortensen and Mahershala Ali.

winners.title: The Shape of Water
winners.description: Del Toro's Cold War fairy tale about a mute janitor and an amphibious creature.

winners.title: Moonlight
winners.description: Three chapters of one life in Miami, and the most famous envelope mix-up in Oscar history.

winners.title: Spotlight
winners.description: The Boston Globe investigation that exposed systemic abuse in the Catholic Church.

winners.title: Birdman
winners.description: A washed-up superhero actor stages a Broadway comeback in one seemingly unbroken take.
